name: Lucian
credit: Lucian of Samosata, engraving by William Faithorne after an imagined likeness (17th century); no authentic portrait survives · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Lucian is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 2nd century AD.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the first volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Books I–VI) (Book VI: 164).

poems.title: Book VI, 164
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: To Glaucus, Nereus, and Melicertes, Ino’s son, to the Lord of the Depths, the son of Cronos, and to the Samothracian gods, do I, Lucillius, saved from the deep, offer these locks clipped from my head, for I have nothing else.

poems.title: Book VII, 308
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: My name is Callimachus, and pitiless Hades carried me off when I was five years old and knew not care. Yet weep not for me; but a small share of life was mine and a small share of life’s evil.

poems.title: Book IX, 120
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: A bad man is like a jar with a hole in it. Pour every kindness into him and you have shed it in vain.

poems.title: Book IX, 367
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Thero, the son of Menippus, in his youth wasted his inheritance shamefully on prodigal outlay; but Euctemon, his father’s friend, when he saw that he was already pressed by parching poverty, strove with tears to cheer him, and gave him his daughter to wife with a large dowry. But when wealth got the better of Thero’s wits, he began to live again in the same extravagance, satisfying disgracefully every lust of his vile belly and the parts beneath it. Thus the returning wave of baneful poverty buried Thero the second time, and EKuctemon wept a second time, not for Thero, but for his daughter’s dowry and bed, and learnt that a man who has made ill use of his own substance will not make honest use of another’s.

poems.title: Book X, 26
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Enjoy thy possessions as if about to die, and use thy goods sparingly as if about to live. That man is wise who understands both these commandments, and hath applied a measure both to thrift and unthrift.

poems.title: Book X, 27
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: If thou doest any foul thing it may perchance be hidden from men, but from the gods it shall not be hidden, even if thou but thinkest of it.

poems.title: Book X, 28
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: For men who are fortunate all life is short, but for those who fall into misfortune one night is infinite time.

poems.title: Book X, 29
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: It is not Love that wrongs the race of men, but Love is an excuse for the souls of the dissolute.

poems.title: Book X, 31
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: All that belongs to mortals is mortal, and all things pass us by; or if not, we pass them by.

poems.title: Book X, 35
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: If thou art fortunate thou art dear to men and dear to gods, and readily they hear thy prayers; but if thou meetest with ill-fortune thou hast no longer any friend, but everything goes against thee, changing with the gusts of fortune.

poems.title: Book X, 36
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Nothing more noxious hath Nature produced among men than the man who simulates pure friendship; for we are no longer on our guard against him as an enemy, but love him as a friend, and thus suffer more injury.

poems.title: Book X, 37
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Slow-footeed counsel is much the best, for swift counsel ever drags repentance behind it.

poems.title: Book X, 41
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: The wealth of the soul is the only true wealth ; the rest has more trouble than the possessions are worth. Him one may rightly call lord of many possessions and wealthy who is able to use his riches. But if a man wears himself out over accounts, ever eager to heap wealth on wealth, his labour shall be like that of the bee in its many-celled honeycomb, for others shall gather the honey.

poems.title: Book X, 42
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Let a seal be set on the tongue concerning words that should not be spoken; for it is better to guard speech than to guard wealth.

poems.title: Book XI, 274
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Tell me, I ask you, Hermes, how did the soul of Lollianus go down to the house of Persephone? If in silence, it was a marvel, and very likely he wanted to teach you also something. Heavens, to think of meeting that man even when one is dead!

poems.title: Book XI, 396
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: You often sent me wine and I was often grateful to you, enjoying the draught of sweet nectar. But now if you love me, don’t send any, for I don’t wish for such wine, not having now any lettuces.

poems.title: Book XI, 397
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Artemidorus, reckoning his fortune at many times ten thousand, and spending nothing, leads the life of mules, who often, carrying on their backs a heavy and precious load of gold, only eat hay.

poems.title: Book XI, 400
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Hail, Grammar, giver of life! Hail, thou whose cure for famine is “Sing, O goddess, the wrath” Men should build a splendid temple to thee, too, and an altar never lacking sacrifice. “For the ways are full of thee, and the sea and its harbours are full of thee,” Grammar, the hostess of all.

poems.title: Book XI, 401
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: A physician sent me his dear son to be taught by me those elementary lessons. And when he had read «Sing the Wrath” and “ imposed a thousand woes, ’ and the third verse that follows these, “ Many strong souls he sped to Hades,” his father no longer sends him to learn from me, but on seeing me said: “All thanks to you, my friend, but the boy ean learn that at home, for I speed down many souls to Hades, and for that I have no need of a grammarian.”

poems.title: Book XI, 402
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: May none of the gods, Erasistratus, create for me that luxury in which you riot, monstrously eating plagues of the stomach worse than famine, such as I wish the children of my enemies might eat. I would starve again even more than I used to starve rather than gorge myself with the luxuries of your table.

poems.title: Book XI, 403
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Paton’s heading: “To the Gout”.
poems.text: Goddess who hatest the poor, sole vanquisher of wealth, who ever knowest to live well, even though it is thy joy to sit on the feet of others, thou knowest how to wear felt, and thou art fond of ointments. A garland delights thee and draughts of Italian wine. These things are never found among the poor. Therefore thou fliest the brassless threshold of poverty, and delightest to come to the feet of wealth.

poems.title: Book XI, 404
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Diophantes with the hydrocele, when he wants to cross to the other side, never gets into the ferry-boat, but putting all his packages and his donkey on the hydrocele, sails across hoisting a sheet. So that in vain have the Tritons glory in the waters if a man with a hydrocele can do the same.

poems.title: Book XI, 405
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Crook-Nosed Nicon has an admirable nose for wine, but he can’t tell quickly what it is like, for scarcely in three summer hours does he smell it himself, since his nose is two hundred cubits long. O what a huge nose! When he crosses a river he often catches little fish with it.

poems.title: Book XI, 408
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: You dye your hair, but you will never dye your old age, or smooth out the wrinkles of your cheeks. Then don’t plaster all your face with white lead, so that you have not a face, but a mask; for it serves no purpose. Why are you out of your wits? Rouge and paste will never turn Hecuba into Helen.

poems.title: Book XI, 410
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: We saw at supper the great wisdom of the Cynic, that bearded beggar with the staff. To begin with he abstained from pulse and radishes, saying that virtue should not be the belly’s slave. But when he saw before his eyes a snow-white sow’s womb with sharp sauce, a dish that soon stole away his prudent mind, he asked for some unexpectedly, and really started eating, saying that a sow’s womb does no harm to virtue.

poems.title: Book XI, 427
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: The exorcist with the stinking mouth cast out many devils by speaking, not by the virtue of his exorcisms, but by that of dung.

poems.title: Book XI, 428
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Way do you wash in vain your Indian body? Give up that device. You cannot shed the sunlight on dark night.

poems.title: Book XI, 429
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Acindynus wished to keep sober when all the others were drunk ; therefore he was the only man who was thought to be drunk.

poems.title: Book XI, 430
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: If you think that to grow a beard is to acquire wisdom, a goat with a fine beard is at once a complete Plato.

poems.title: Book XI, 431
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: If you are quick at eating and tardy in running, eat with your feet and run with your mouth.

poems.title: Book XI, 432
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: A Foot put out the lamp when he was bitten by many fleas, saying: “ You can’t see me any longer.”

poems.title: Book XI, 433
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: Painter, thou stealest the form only, and canst not, trusting in thy colours, capture the voice.

poems.title: Book XI, 434
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: If you see a hairless head, breast, and shoulders, make no enquiries ; it is a bald fool that you see.

poems.title: Book XI, 435
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: It strikes me as wonderful how Bytus is a sophist, since he has neither common speech nor reason.

poems.title: Book XI, 436
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: You will sooner find white crows and winged tortoises than a Cappadocian who is an accomplished orator.

poems.title: Book XVI, 154: On the Same
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: This Echo of the rocks thou seest, my friend, the companion of Pan, singing back to us a responsive note, the garrulous counterfeit of every kind of tongue, the shepherds’ sweet toy. After hearing every word thou utterest, begone.

poems.title: Book XVI, 163: On the Same
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: None ever saw the Paphian naked, bul if anyone did, it is this man who here erected the naked Paphian.

poems.title: Book XVI, 164
poems.author: Lucian
poems.text: To thee, Cypris, I dedicate the beautiful image of thy form, since I have nothing better than thy form.

poems.title: On a Child of Five (Mackail)
poems.author: Lucian
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Me Callimachus, a five-years-old child whose spirit knew not grief, pitiless Death snatched away; but weep thou not for me; for little was my share in life, and little in life's ills.

poems.title: The Fruits of Philosophy (Mackail)
poems.author: Lucian
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: We saw at dinner the great wisdom of that sturdy beggar the Cynic with the long beard; for at first he abstained from lupines and radishes, saying that Virtue ought not to be a slave to the belly; but when he saw a snowy womb dressed with sharp sauce before his eyes, which at once stole away his sagacious intellect, he unexpectedly asked for it, and ate of it heartily, observing that an entrée could not harm Virtue.

poems.title: The World's Revenge (Mackail)
poems.author: Lucian
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: In a company where all were drunk, Acindynus must needs be sober; and so he seemed himself the one drunk man there.

poems.title: The Way of the World (Mackail)
poems.author: Lucian
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Mortal is what belongs to mortals, and all things pass by us; and if not, yet we pass by them.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.308: παῖδά με πενταέτηρον, ἀκηδέα θυμὸν ἔχοντα,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
παῖδά με πενταέτηρον, ἀκηδέα θυμὸν ἔχοντα,
νηλειὴς Ἀίδης ἥρπασε Καλλίμαχον.
ἀλλά με μὴ κλαίοις· καὶ γὰρ βιότοιο μετέσχον
παύρου, καὶ παύρων τῶν βιότοιο κακῶν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.120: φαῦλος ἀνὴρ πίθος ἐστὶ τετρημένος, εἰς ὃν ἁπάσας
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
φαῦλος ἀνὴρ πίθος ἐστὶ τετρημένος, εἰς ὃν ἁπάσας
ἀντλῶν τὰς χάριτας, εἰς κενὸν ἐξέχεας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.367: τὸν πατρικὸν πλοῦτον νέος ὢν Θήρων ὁ Μενίππου
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
τὸν πατρικὸν πλοῦτον νέος ὢν Θήρων ὁ Μενίππου
αἰσχρῶς εἰς ἀκρατεῖς ἐξέχεεν δαπάνας·
ἀλλά μιν Εὐκτήμων, πατρικὸς φίλος, ὡς ἐνόησεν
ἤδη καρφαλέῃ τειρόμενον πενίῃ,
καί μιν δακρυχέων ἀνελάμβανε, καὶ πόσιν αὐτὸν
θῆκε θυγατρὸς ἑῆς, πόλλʼ ἐπὶ μείλια δούς.
αὐτάρ ἐπεὶ Θήρωνα περὶ φρένας ἤλυθε πλοῦτος,
αὐτίκα ταῖς αὐταῖς ἐτρέφετʼ ἐν δαπάναις,
γαστρὶ χαριζόμενος πᾶσαν χάριν οὐ κατὰ κόσμον,
τῇ θʼ ὑπὸ τὴν μιαρὰν γαστέρα μαργοσύνῃ.
οὕτως μὲν Θήρωνα τὸ δεύτερον ἀμφεκάλυψεν
οὐλομένης πενίης κῦμα παλιρρόθιον.
Εὐκτήμων δʼ ἐδάκρυσε τὸ δεύτερον, οὐκέτι κεῖνον,
ἀλλὰ θυγατρὸς ἑῆς προῖκά τε καὶ θάλαμον.
ἔγνω δʼ ὡς οὐκ ἔστι κακῶς κεχρημένον ἄνδρα
τοῖς ἰδίοις εἶναι πιστὸν ἐν ἀλλοτρίοις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.26: ὡς τεθνηξόμενος τῶν σῶν ἀγαθῶν ἀπόλαυε,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ὡς τεθνηξόμενος τῶν σῶν ἀγαθῶν ἀπόλαυε,
ὡς δὲ βιωσόμενος φείδεο σῶν κτεάνων.
ἔστι δʼ ἀνὴρ σοφὸς οὗτος, ὃς ἄμφω ταῦτα νοήσας
φειδοῖ καὶ δαπάνῃ μέτρον ἐφηρμόσατο.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.27: ἀνθρώπους μὲν ἴσως λήσεις ἄτοπόν τι ποιήσας,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ἀνθρώπους μὲν ἴσως λήσεις ἄτοπόν τι ποιήσας,
οὐ λήσεις δὲ θεοὺς οὐδὲ λογιζόμενος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.28: τοῖσι μὲν εὖ πράττουσιν πᾶς ὁ βίος βραχύς; ἐστιν,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
τοῖσι μὲν εὖ πράττουσιν πᾶς ὁ βίος βραχύς; ἐστιν,
τοῖς δὲ κακῶς μία νὺξ ἄπλετός ἐστι χρόνος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.29: οὐχ ὁ Ἔρως ἀδικεῖ μερόπων γένος, ἀλλʼ ἀκολάστοις
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
οὐχ ὁ Ἔρως ἀδικεῖ μερόπων γένος, ἀλλʼ ἀκολάστοις
ψυχαῖς ἀνθρώπων ἔσθʼ ὁ Ἔρως πρόφασις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.31: θνητὰ τὰ τῶν θνητῶν, καὶ πάντα παρέρχεται ἡμᾶς
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
θνητὰ τὰ τῶν θνητῶν, καὶ πάντα παρέρχεται ἡμᾶς
ἢν δὲ μή, ἀλλʼ ἡμεῖς αὐτὰ παρερχόμεθα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.35: εὖ πράττων, φίλος εἶ θνητοῖς, φίλος εἶ μακάρεσσι,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
εὖ πράττων, φίλος εἶ θνητοῖς, φίλος εἶ μακάρεσσι,
καί σευ ῥηιδίως ἔκλυον εὐξαμένου·
ἢν πταίσῃς, οὐδεὶς ἔτι σοι φίλος, ἀλλʼ ἅμα πάντα
ἐχθρά, Τύχης ῥιπαῖς συμμεταβαλλόμενα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.36: οὐδὲν ἐν ἀνθρώποισι Φύσις χαλεπώτερον εὗρεν
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
οὐδὲν ἐν ἀνθρώποισι Φύσις χαλεπώτερον εὗρεν
ἀνθρώπου καθαρὰν ψευδομένου φιλίην
οὐ γὰρ ἔθʼ ὡς ἐχθρὸν προφυλασσόμεθʼ, ἀλλʼ ἀγαπῶντες
ὡς φίλον, ἐν τούτῳ πλείονα βλαπτόμεθα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.37: ἡ βραδύπους βουλὴ μέγʼ ἀμείνων ἡ δὲ ταχεῖα
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ἡ βραδύπους βουλὴ μέγʼ ἀμείνων ἡ δὲ ταχεῖα
αἰὲν ἐφελκομένη τὴν μετάνοιαν ἔχει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.41: πλοῦτος ὁ τῆς ψυχῆς πλοῦτος μόνος ἐστὶν ἀληθής·
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
πλοῦτος ὁ τῆς ψυχῆς πλοῦτος μόνος ἐστὶν ἀληθής·
τἆλλα δʼ ἔχει λύπην πλείονα τῶν κτεάνων.
τόνδε πολυκτέανον καὶ πλούσιον ἐστι δίκαιον
κλῄζειν, ὃς χρῆσθαι τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς δύναται.
εἰ δέ τις ἐν ψήφοις κατατήκεται, ἄλλον ἐπʼ ἄλλῳ
σωρεύειν αἰεὶ πλοῦτον ἐπειγόμενος,
οὗτος ὁποῖα μέλισσα πολυτρήτοις ἐνὶ σίμβλοις
μοχθήσει, ἑτέρων δρεπτομένων τὸ μέλι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.42: ἀρρήτων ἐπέων γλώσσῃ σφραγὶς ἐπικείσθω·
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ἀρρήτων ἐπέων γλώσσῃ σφραγὶς ἐπικείσθω·
κρείσσων γὰρ μύθων ἢ κτεάνων φυλακή.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.274: εἰπέ μοι εἰρομένῳ, Κυλλήνιε, πῶς κατέβαινεν
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
εἰπέ μοι εἰρομένῳ, Κυλλήνιε, πῶς κατέβαινεν
Λολλιανοῦ ψυχὴ δῶμα τὸ Φερσεφόνης ;
θαῦμα μέν, εἰ σιγῶσα· τυχὸν δέ τι καὶ σὲ διδάσκειν
ἤθελε. φεῦ, κείνου καὶ νέκυν ἀντιάσαι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.396: πολλάκις οἶνον ἔπεμψας ἐμοί, καὶ πολλάκις ἔγνων
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
πολλάκις οἶνον ἔπεμψας ἐμοί, καὶ πολλάκις ἔγνων
σοὶ χάριν, ἡδυπότῳ νέκταρι τερπόμενος.
νῦν δʼ εἴπερ με φιλεῖς, μὴ πέμψῃς· οὐ δέομαι γὰρ
οἴνου τοιούτου, μηκέτʼ ἔχων θρίδακας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.397: πολλὰς μυριάδας ψηφίζων Ἀρτεμίδωρος,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
πολλὰς μυριάδας ψηφίζων Ἀρτεμίδωρος,
καὶ μηδὲν δαπανῶν, ζῇ βίον ἡμιόνων,
πολλάκις αἳ χρυσοῦ τιμαλφέα φόρτον ἔχουσαι
πολλὸν ὑπὲρ νώτου, χόρτον ἔδουσι μόνον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.400: ἵλαθι, Γραμματικὴ φυσίζοε, ἵλαθι λιμοῦ
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ἵλαθι, Γραμματικὴ φυσίζοε, ἵλαθι λιμοῦ
φάρμακον εὑρομένη μῆνιν ἄειδε θεά.
νηὸν ἐχρῆν καὶ σοὶ περικαλλέα δωμήσασθαι,
καὶ βωμὸν θυέων μή ποτε δευόμενον.
καὶ γὰρ σοῦ μεσταὶ μὲν ὁδοί, μεστὴ δὲ θάλασσα
καὶ λιμένες, πάντων δέκτρια Γραμματική.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.401: ἰητήρ τις ἐμοὶ τὸν ἑὸν φίλον υἱὸν ἔπεμψεν,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ἰητήρ τις ἐμοὶ τὸν ἑὸν φίλον υἱὸν ἔπεμψεν,
ὥστε μαθεῖν παρʼ ἐμοὶ ταῦτα τὰ γραμματικά.
ὡς δὲ τὸ μῆνιν ἄειδε καὶ “ ἄλγεα μυρίʼ ἔθηκεν
” ἔγνω, καὶ τὸ τρίτον τοῖσδʼ ἀκόλουθον ἔπος
πολλὰς δʼ ἰφθίμους ψυχὰς Ἄϊδι προΐαψεν,
οὐκέτι μιν πέμπει πρός με μαθησόμενον.
ἀλλὰ μʼ ἰδὼν ὁ πατήρ, σοὶ μὲν χάρις, εἶπεν, “ἑταῖρε·
αὐτὰρ ὁ παῖς παρʼ ἐμοὶ ταῦτα μαθεῖν δύναται·
καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ πολλὰς ψυχὰς Ἄϊδι προϊάπτω,
καὶ πρὸς τοῦτʼ οὐδὲν γραμματικοῦ δέομαι.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.402: μηδείς μοι ταύτην, Ἐρασίστρατε, τὴν σπατάλην σου
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
μηδείς μοι ταύτην, Ἐρασίστρατε, τὴν σπατάλην σου
ποιήσειε θεῶν, ᾗ σὺ κατασπαταλᾷς,
ἔσθων ἐκτραπέλως στομάχων κακά, χείρονα λιμοῦ,
οἷα φάγοιεν ἐμῶν ἀντιδίκων τεκνία.
πεινάσαιμι γὰρ αὖθις ἔτι πλέον, ἢ πρὶν ἐπείνων,
ἢ χορτασθείην τῆς παρὰ σοὶ σπατάλης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.403: Μισόπτωχε θεά, μούνη πλούτου δαμάτειρα,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
Μισόπτωχε θεά, μούνη πλούτου δαμάτειρα,
ἡ τὸ καλῶς ζῆσαι πάντοτʼ ἐπισταμένη,
εἰ δὲ καὶ ἀλλοτρίοις ἐπιιζομένη ποσὶ χαίρεις,
πιλοφορεῖν τʼ οἶδας, καὶ μύρα σοι μέλεται,
τέρπει καὶ στέφανός σε, καὶ Αὐσονίου πόμα Βάκχου.
ταῦτα παρὰ πτωχοῖς γίνεται οὐδέποτε.
τοὔνεκα νῦν φεύγεις πενίης τὸν ἀχάλκεον οὐδόν,
τέρπᾐ δʼ αὖ πλούτου πρὸς πόδας ἐρχομένη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.404: οὐδέποτʼ εἰς πορθμεῖον ὁ κηλήτης Διόφαντος
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
οὐδέποτʼ εἰς πορθμεῖον ὁ κηλήτης Διόφαντος
ἐμβαίνει μέλλων εἰς τὸ πέραν ἀπίναι·
τῆς κήλης δʼ ἐπάνωθε τὰ φορτία πάντα τεθεικὼς
καὶ τὸν ὄνον, διαπλεῖ σινδόνʼ ἐπαράμενος.
ὥστε μάτην Τρίτωνες ἐν ὕδασι δόξαν ἔχουσιν,
εἰ καὶ κηλήτης ταὐτὸ ποιεῖν δύναται.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.405: ὁ γρυπὸς Νίκων ὀσφραίνεται οἴνου ἄριστα,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ὁ γρυπὸς Νίκων ὀσφραίνεται οἴνου ἄριστα,
οὐ δύναται δʼ εἰπεῖν οἷος ἂν ᾖ ταχέως.
ἐν τρισὶν ὥραις γὰρ θεριναῖς μόλις αἰσθάνετʼ αὐτὸς,
ὡς ἂν ἔχων πηχῶν ῥῖνα διακοσίων.
ὦ μεγάλου μυκτῆρος· ὅταν ποταμὸν διαβαίνῃ,
θηρεύει τούτῳ πολλάκις ἰχθύδια.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.410: τοῦ πωγωνοφόρου κυνικοῦ, τοῦ βακτροπροσαίτου,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
τοῦ πωγωνοφόρου κυνικοῦ, τοῦ βακτροπροσαίτου,
εἴδομεν ἐν δείπνῳ τὴν μεγάλην σοφίαν.
θέρμων μὲν γὰρ πρῶτον ἀπέσχετο καὶ ῥαφανίδων,
μὴ δεῖν δουλεύειν γαστρὶ λέγων ἀρετήν.
εὖτε δʼ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖσιν ἴδεν χιονώδεα βόλβαν
στρυφνήν, ἣ πινυτὸν ἤδη ἔκλεπτε νόον,
ᾔτησεν παρὰ προσδοκίαν, καὶ ἔτρωγεν ἀληθῶς,
κοὐδὲν ἔφη βόλβαν τὴν ἀρετὴν ἀδικεῖν,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.427: δαίμονα πολλὰ λαλῶν ὀζόστομος ἐξορκιστὴς
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
δαίμονα πολλὰ λαλῶν ὀζόστομος ἐξορκιστὴς
ἐξέβαλʼ, οὐχ ὅρκων, ἀλλὰ κόπρων δυνάμει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.428: εἰς τί μάτην νίπτεις δέμας Ἰνδικόν; ἴσχεο τέχνης·
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
εἰς τί μάτην νίπτεις δέμας Ἰνδικόν; ἴσχεο τέχνης·
οὐ δύνασαι δνοφερὴν νύκτα καθηλιάσαι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.429: ἐν πᾶσιν μεθύουσιν Ἀκινδυνος ἤθελε νήφειν,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ἐν πᾶσιν μεθύουσιν Ἀκινδυνος ἤθελε νήφειν,
τοὔνεκα καὶ μεθύειν αὐτὸς ἔδοξε μόνος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.430: εἰ τὸ τρέφειν πώγωνα δοκεῖς σοφίαν περιποιεῖν,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
εἰ τὸ τρέφειν πώγωνα δοκεῖς σοφίαν περιποιεῖν,
καὶ τράγος εὐπώγων αἶψʼ ὅλος ˘ ἐστὶ Πλάτων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.431: εἰ ταχὺς εἰς τὸ φαγεῖν καὶ πρὸς δρόμον ἀμβλὺς ὑπάρχεις
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
εἰ ταχὺς εἰς τὸ φαγεῖν καὶ πρὸς δρόμον ἀμβλὺς ὑπάρχεις
τοῖς ποσί σου τρῶγε, καὶ τρέχε τῷ στόματι,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.432: ἔσβεσε τὸν λύχνον μῶρος, ψυλλῶν ὑπὸ πολλῶν
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ἔσβεσε τὸν λύχνον μῶρος, ψυλλῶν ὑπὸ πολλῶν
δακνόμενος, λέξας· οὐκέτι με βλέπετε.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.433: ζωγράφε, τὰς μορφὰς κλέπτεις μόνον οὐ δύνασαι δὲ
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ζωγράφε, τὰς μορφὰς κλέπτεις μόνον οὐ δύνασαι δὲ
φωνὴν συλῆσαι χρώματι πειθόμενος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.434: ἢν ἐσίδῃς κεφαλὴν μαδαράν, καὶ στέρνα,, καὶ ὤμους,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ἢν ἐσίδῃς κεφαλὴν μαδαράν, καὶ στέρνα,, καὶ ὤμους,
μηδὲν ἐρωτήσῃς· μῶρον ὁρᾷς φαλακρόν,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.435: θαυμάζειν μοι ἔπεισιν, ὅπως Βύτος ἐστὶ σοφιστὴς,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
θαυμάζειν μοι ἔπεισιν, ὅπως Βύτος ἐστὶ σοφιστὴς,
οὔτε λόγον κοινόν, οὔτε λογισμὸν ἔχων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.436: θᾶττον ἔην λευκοὺς κόρακας πτηνάς τε χελώνας
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
θᾶττον ἔην λευκοὺς κόρακας πτηνάς τε χελώνας
εὑρεῖν, ἢ δόκιμον ῥήτορα Καππαδόκην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.163: τὴν Παφίην γυμνὴν οὐδεὶς ἴδεν εἰ δέ τις εἶδεν,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
τὴν Παφίην γυμνὴν οὐδεὶς ἴδεν εἰ δέ τις εἶδεν,
οὗτος ὁ τὴν γυμνὴν στησάμενος Παφίην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.164: σοὶ μορφῆς ἀνέθηκα τεῆς περικαλλὲς ἄγαλμα,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
σοὶ μορφῆς ἀνέθηκα τεῆς περικαλλὲς ἄγαλμα,
Κύπρι, τεῆς μορφῆς φέρτερον οὐδὲν ἔχων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.17: αἱ τρισσαί τοι ταῦτα τὰ παίγνια θῆκαν ἑταῖραι,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
αἱ τρισσαί τοι ταῦτα τὰ παίγνια θῆκαν ἑταῖραι,
Κύπρι μάκαιρʼ, ἄλλης ἄλλη ἀπʼ ἐργασίης·
ὧν ἀπὸ μὲν πυγῆς Εὐφρὼ τάδε, ταῦτα δὲ Κλειὼ
ὡς θέμις, ἡ τριτάτη δʼ Ἀτθὶς ἀπʼ οὐρανίων.
ἀνθʼ ὧν τῇ μὲν πέμπε τὰ παιδικά, δεσπότι, κέρδη,
τῇ δὲ τὰ θηλείης, τῇ δὲ τὰ μηδετέρης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.122: πολλὰ τὸ δαιμόνιον δύναται, κἂν ᾖ παράδοξα·
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
πολλὰ τὸ δαιμόνιον δύναται, κἂν ᾖ παράδοξα·
τοὺς μικροὺς ἀνάγει, τοὺς μεγάλους κατάγει·
καὶ σοῦ τὴν ὀφρὺν καὶ τὸν τῦφον καταπαύσει,
κἂν ποταμὸς χρυσοῦ νάματά σοι παρέχῃ.
οὐ θρύον, οὐ μαλάχην ἄνεμός ποτε, τὰς δὲ μεγίστας
ἢ δρύας ἢ πλατάνους οἶδε χαμαὶ κατάγειν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.294: πλοῦτον μὲν πλουτοῦντος ἔχεις, ψυχὴν δὲ πένητος,
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
πλοῦτον μὲν πλουτοῦντος ἔχεις, ψυχὴν δὲ πένητος,
ὦ τοῖς κληρονόμοις πλούσιε, σοὶ δὲ πένης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.238: ὧδε Πρίηπον
poems.author: Lucian
poems.note: Greek text of an epigram ascribed to Lucian (Perseus files it as Pseudo-Lucianus); W. R. Paton, The Greek Anthology, Loeb Classical Library, 1916-18.
poems.text:
ὧδε Πρίηπον
Εὐτυχίδης, ξηρῶν κληματίδων φύλακα·
καὶ περιβέβλημαι κρημνὸν βαθύν. ὃς
δʼ ἂν ἐπέλθῃ,
οὐδὲν ἔχει κλέψαι πλὴν ἐμὲ τὸν φύλακα.
